questions.prompt: What is the extra day in a leap year?
questions.explanation: A leap year adds 29 February, taking the year from 365 days to 366.

questions.prompt: Why does the calendar sometimes need an extra day?
options: A year of seasons is a little longer than 365 days
questions.explanation: The small amount of time beyond 365 days adds up. Leap days help keep calendar dates in step with the seasons.

questions.prompt: Why will 2100 not be a leap year?
options: All years ending in 00 lose the day
It ends in 00 but does not divide exactly by 400
questions.explanation: Years ending in 00 have an extra check. 2100 is five groups of 400 plus 100 left over, so it skips the leap day.

sections.title: What is a leap day?
sections.html:
Most calendar years have 365 days. A leap year has 366. The extra day is 29 February.

We need that extra day because a year of seasons is a little longer than 365 days: almost another quarter of a day. If we ignored that leftover time every year, our calendar would slowly slip away from the seasons.

Adding a day roughly every four years helps the calendar keep up.

sections.title: Why “every four years” is not the whole story
sections.html:
The leftover time is a little less than a quarter of a day. Adding a whole day every four years therefore adds slightly too much.

The calendar fixes this by leaving out a few leap days. The extra rule applies to years ending in 00, such as 1900, 2000 and 2100.

These rules belong to the Gregorian calendar, the calendar widely used for everyday dates today.

sections.title: Follow the checks one at a time
sections.html:
First, a small maths phrase: “divisible by four” means you can split a number into groups of four with nothing left over. For example, 12 makes three complete groups of four; 13 leaves one over.

  1. Can the year number be divided by 4 with nothing left over? If no, it is not a leap year. If yes, continue.
  2. Does the year end in 00? If no, it is a leap year. If yes, there is one last check.
  3. Can it be divided by 400 with nothing left over? If yes, keep the leap day. If no, skip it.

sections.title: Compare 2000 and 2100
sections.html:
Both years end in 00, so check groups of 400
YearGroups of 400Leap day?
2000Five complete groups; nothing left overYes
2100Five complete groups, with 100 left overNo
2400Six complete groups; nothing left overYes

That is why 2100 will not have 29 February. It does pass the four-year check, but fails the extra check for years ending in 00.

sections.title: An old date needs one extra question
sections.html:
Countries did not all start using this calendar at once. When reading about an old event, ask which calendar was in use there.

Next, see what happened when Britain changed its calendar in 1752. The date jumped, but people did not lose eleven days of their lives.
